title: Apple’s first smart display is the 7-inch HomeView for $299
gist: Apple opened preorders for HomeView, its first smart display, a 7-inch A18-powered hub at $299 launching November 13 that leans on Siri AI and iCloud+ camera features. Wall mounting costs extra and comes in only two colors.

insights.claim: Apple's HomeView is a 7-inch smart display and speaker, priced $299, preordering now and launching November 13, competing with the Amazon Echo Show.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Apple enters the smart-display category directly against Amazon's Echo Show.

insights.claim: HomeView runs an A18 chip with a Liquid Retina LCD screen of 0.3 to 500 nits and a tilting stainless steel hinge over a speaker base.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Reuse of phone silicon indicates A-series chips extend into home devices.

insights.claim: Wall mounting needs a specific mount made by Schneider Home starting at $60, available in only two of four colors, with custom drivers tuned for wall mounting.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding

insights.claim: HomeView supports up to six family members, identifies the user by camera to show their profile, and links to an Apple Intelligence iPhone or iPad for Messages, Calendar, Reminders and FaceTime.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Home hub ties device value to the iPhone ecosystem.

insights.claim: The most advanced recognition of people, pets, packages and vehicles and video descriptions require a supported iCloud+ subscription and compatible cameras.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Apple is using hardware to pull through recurring iCloud+ services revenue.

insights.claim: Users without an Apple Intelligence iPhone or iPad still get Siri AI's broad world knowledge and conversation, with requests run locally or via Private Cloud Compute, which Apple says does not store data or make it accessible to anyone.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Apple positions privacy-preserving AI as differentiator versus Amazon and Google in the home.
